article.title: House Negro
article.author: Desi Cortez
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Is Congressman Hakeem Jeffries the leader of the House Democrats, or is he becoming the modern political embodiment of Malcolm X’s House Negro : a man so comfortable inside the Big House that he mistakes proximity to power for possession of it? I suggest it’s the latter…. Before establishment Democrats faint into their cashmere handkerchiefs, please spare me lectures about decorum and refinement. I'm questioning if Jeffries' political backbone is made of the same claymation stuff Gumby and Pokeys were made of. I’m not dissecting his résumé. I'm questioning whether the man preparing to become America's first Black Speaker understands that sitting in the master's chair isn't the same as kicking the master out of it. Can I get an Aman! Because too many Democrats have become lawn-jockey caretakers of a house that should have been condemned decades ago. On November 10, they offered another miserable demonstration of their talent for losing a fight while announcing their determination to win it. Eleven Empty Chairs and One Happy Warlord The Republican-controlled House voted 211–204 to send eight articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth to committee, effectively burying a showdown over Trump's swaggering Pentagon commander. All 203 Democrats who voted opposed the maneuver. Jeffries opposed it. Republican Thomas Massie, who introduced the articles, opposed it. Eleven Democrats didn't vote. Eleven! Had all eleven voted no, the referral motion would have failed, 215–211. Apparently, the Democratic Party can coordinate galas, donor receptions, campaign junkets, television interviews and enough luncheons to feed half of Delaware. But organizing eleven members to cast votes in a showdown requires technology unavailable since the 1969 moon landing. Among the absent was former Speaker Nancy Pelosi, celebrated for knowing where every vote was hiding. How deliciously appropriate that a party famous for fundraising prowess came up short on the one currency Congress needed. Related: America, Satan Called and He Wants His Baby Brother Back I don't pretend every absence was frivolous. The outcome was real, the arithmetic unforgiving, and the failure a political embarrassment. MAGA didn't have to win a moral argument. It had to count the empty chairs. And our gallant opposition supplied them. A Hard Yes With a Soft Landing Jeffries declared himself a “hard yes” on Hegseth's impeachment. Splendid. He voted accordingly. Terrific. But leadership isn't an attendance award for pressing a button. It's getting your troops onto the battlefield when battle matters. Jeffries is minority leader, soon to be positioned for the Speaker's gavel after the Democrats' midterm victory. He wants the highest seat in the House. He ought to demonstrate he can manage the seats his caucus already occupies. Asked about the missing Democrats, he indicated he hadn't spoken with his floor team about the failure. Bullshit! Congressman, that's where you should begin your investigation into America's great disappearing opposition. Republicans count votes like casino operators count chips. They know what power is for. Too many Democrats treat votes like dinner reservations: show up if convenient, cancel without penalty, and send regrets about the fragile state of democracy. The Republican machine arrives with bulldozers. The Democratic leadership arrives with laminated guidelines on courteous resistance. And then wonders why the building is gone. I’m so sick n’ tired of being sick n’ tired of these political pimps and prostitutes I could vomit…. Peep this: Jeffries wants America to believe he is MAGA’s mortal enemy, yet in August he slipped into a private New York meeting with Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law and unofficial diplomatic fixer. Former Obama aide Tommy Vietor blasted Kushner’s Gulf-money dealings; Mehdi Hasan said the only proper meeting involved a subpoena. Meanwhile, OpenSecrets estimates Jeffries received $1.74 million from pro-Israel donors through 2024, with AIPAC-linked contributions continuing into 2026. Related: Political Extinction of Biblical Proportions: Democrats, Never Forgive and Forget! These accusations ricochet through progressive coffee shops, backyard parties and paddle boy courts, raising concerns about something much more sinister than a secret payoff: establishment intimacy, donor influence, and whose interests Jeffries serves. He promises voters resistance while offering the politically connected access. Is this the opposition party, or a VIP lounge with a plush blue carpet? A Republican Brought the Charges Here's the scandal inside the embarrassment: the impeachment resolution came from Thomas Massie, a conservative Republican from Kentucky. I ask why o’ why did a Republican have to initiate this confrontation with Hegseth? Massie's eight articles accused the defense secretary of abusing authority over military action, including the Iran war, and other conduct. Those accusations deserved a public reckoning, not a paper coffin in committee. Massie brought the charges. Jeffries brought his declaration of support. Eleven Democrats brought no recorded vote. Hegseth wasn't acquitted. He escaped an impeachment proceeding through a procedural maneuver. But MAGA knows how to market a procedural escape as divine vindication. Trump can convert a missing shoelace into a victory parade; imagine what he can do with eleven missing Democrats. And our opposition provided the confetti. What makes this galling is that Democrats claim to be the firewall against Trump's excesses. A firewall? This one comes with a revolving door, an absentee sheet, and a fundraising link. The Big House Has a New Dress Code Malcolm X used the contrast between the House Negro and the Field Negro to describe two relationships to power: one invested in the master's comfort, the other determined to escape the master's control. That distinction stings because the political Big House is overflowing with people who confuse access with independence. They know the donor's preferred wine, the lobbyist's number, the proper political “angle” for a television interview, and how to say “we stand with working families” while checking whether the statement will offend aristocrats and fatcats on Wall Street. The plantation's wardrobe has changed. The cotton fields have given way to corporate boardrooms, private equity portfolios, tax shelters, giant warehouses, and a campaign-finance system that turns public service into a subscription plan. Today's overseers don't need horses. They have consultants, algorithms, legal departments, and lobbyists to populate a small state like Wyoming or Rhode Island. And establishment Democrats? Often they climax when they receive an invitation into the Big House to see Sweet Daddy Donny. They're told to be realistic. To protect swing districts. To respect institutions. To avoid frightening donors. To find common ground with men who treat compromise as an opportunity to pick somebody's pocket. By the time Democrats finish examining the etiquette of throwing a punch, MAGA has stolen the boxing gloves, sold the arena, and charged the spectators for parking. That's not leadership. That's cotton plantation management with a congressional pension. It’s not that they can’t fight, they don’t want to. Related: Let Them Eat Touchdowns! The NFL Meets the French Revolution DINOs, Blue Dogs, and the Gospel of Surrender I call this infestation DINOs: Democrats In Name Only. These folks, of all walks of life, aren’t Democrats; they’re Private Lear Jet Capitalists These specimens have perfected the art of appearing concerned while staying still. Yes, they can be so very quiet, you can hear an orange rat piss on cotton…. Performative Democrats can transform outrage into a press release, a press release into a listening session, a listening session into a task force, and a task force into an election-year promise to study the outrage. They don't extinguish fires. They commission surveys about whether the smoke is popular among moderate voters. The disease predates Jeffries. Reagan's trickle-down economics taught America to shower the rich with money and call the trickle prosperity . The wealthy got swimming pools. Worker ants and bees got the water bill. Then came Clinton-era triangulation, corporate-friendly Democrats, and the pilgrimage toward an imaginary political center that moves right every time Republicans clear their throats. The Blue Dogs barked at progressives, wagged their tails at corporate money, and assured working people that sacrifice would deliver prosperity. Whose sacrifice? The factory worker's. The single mother's. The public-school teacher's. The Black and Brown communities are summoned to save Democratic candidates every election, then instructed to be patient while the party reassures its affluent sponsors. Seldom seen, hardly heard. Wall Street loves this arrangement. Republicans deliver the unapologetic robbery. Democrats object to the tone in which the robbery was announced. One party brings the crowbar. Too many members of the other bring a request that the burglars wipe their feet. Don't mistake my impatience for a demand that Democrats become louder versions of Trump. Volume isn't courage. Courage is putting donors on notice, members on the floor, and your signature on a subpoena that makes powerful people sweat through thousand-dollar shirts. It means choosing a side when choosing has consequences, not after a pollster certifies that courage tests well in suburban counties. I seek righteousness, as should we all. But I'll take revenge. Present! The Battle Cry of the Timid Hegseth wasn't the first demonstration. On September 15, Congressman Al Green tried to force a vote on impeaching Trump. Republicans moved to kill the resolution. Jeffries voted present, alongside dozens of Democrats. Present! Not yes. No, no. Present. The equivalent of raising your hand for roll call and crawling underneath the desk when the teacher asks what you believe. Jeffries and his colleagues can recite all the procedural justifications they want. I have watched this movie too many times. In the Democratic version, the opposition spends ninety minutes drafting a sternly worded letter while the villain drives away with the treasury. The Democratic voters who delivered the 2026 midterm victory did not mobilize for another season of theatrical concern. They want subpoenas, oversight, public testimony, congressional muscle, and consequences for misconduct. They want a party that knows the difference between strategic patience and political paralysis. They want elected officials who treat the constitutional separation of powers as something more than an antique displayed behind velvet ropes. They want leaders who understand that winning an election isn't the finish line. It's the starting pistol. Mr. Jeffries, the Field Is on Fire MAGA's genius has been to convince struggling Americans that their enemies are other struggling Americans. Keep poor white workers suspicious of poor Black workers. Keep native-born families suspicious of immigrants. Keep men angry at women, neighbors angry at neighbors, and everybody distracted while the platinum-spoon aristocracy empties the cash register. It's a marvelous racket if you're collecting the checks. And what do the establishment Democrats offer as the counterattack? Another committee. Another consultant. Another solemn announcement that democracy must be defended, preferably without inconveniencing a billionaire before cocktails. Mr. Jeffries, you are preparing to inherit a Democratic majority, not a lifetime achievement trophy. The gavel isn't a souvenir. It's a weapon of accountability, and voters expect you to use it. Demand attendance. Count votes before making promises. Investigate abuses. Compel testimony. Haul the powerful into public hearings. Stop confusing respectful language with meaningful resistance. Stop treating the people who delivered this victory as spectators at the coronation of another Washington insider. History won't remember how elegantly Hakeem Jeffries occupied the master's chair. It'll remember whether he liberated the plantation or became the first Black gentleman trusted to lock the gates from the inside. Congressman, if you're going to spend your political career kissing the master's ring, at least have the decency to stop telling the field hands you're leading a revolution. The question isn't whether Hakeem Jeffries is intelligent, polished, articulate, or significant. The question is whether he intends to challenge power or merely become its most distinguished Black caretaker. Black Americans have spent generations helping this country fulfill promises it made and repeatedly broke. We didn't struggle for the ballot so a politician could win a historic office and use its furniture as a monument to his advancement. Representation without confrontation is a photograph, not liberation. A Black face atop a compromised institution is no substitute for a leader prepared to shake that institution until the loose change and corporate receipts come falling out. I don't want another elegantly dressed manager of the Big House. I don't need another leader who delivers magnificent speeches about the fire while asking the arsonists whether they would prefer bottled or sparkling water. Eleven Democrats were missing. A Republican introduced the impeachment articles. Hegseth escaped the reckoning. And the party promising to confront MAGA supplied the empty chairs. Mr. Jeffries, the field hands didn't fight their way to the ballot box so you could become the master's favorite houseguest. Either tear down the political plantation or get your silk-stocking, silver-polishing ass out of the doorway.
